title: Personal Credit Cards: Earning Rewards Points and Reversing Them on Refunds
content:
Points on Personal Credit Cards are earned only on tiers whose rewards currency is something other than none. This page sets out how a purchase earns points and how points come back off when a purchase is refunded.

## Earning on a purchase

- Each posted purchase earns on its amount in whole dollars; any fraction of a dollar is dropped.
- A purchase in one of the tier's bonus merchant categories earns the bonus rate per dollar while the bonus-category spending already posted in that calendar quarter, before this purchase and net of merchant credits on those purchases, is still below the tier's quarterly bonus ceiling. The part of the purchase that goes beyond the ceiling earns the base rate instead.
- Every other purchase earns the base rate per dollar.
- The resulting points are rounded down to a whole number.
- Nothing is earned on cash advances, balance transfers, fees or interest.

The quarter is the calendar quarter in which the purchase posted.

## Clawback on a merchant credit

When a merchant refunds a purchase, the points that purchase earned are taken back in proportion to the refund, as a points removal linked to the merchant credit.

## Worked examples (illustrative rates, not those of any tier)

Assume a bonus rate of 4 points and a base rate of 1.5 points per dollar, with a quarterly bonus ceiling of 1000.00 USD.

| Purchase | Bonus-category spend already in the quarter | Whole dollars at bonus rate | Whole dollars at base rate | Points |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 57.80 USD, bonus category | 400.00 USD | 57 | 0 | 228 |
| 60.00 USD, bonus category | 980.00 USD | 20 | 40 | 80 at bonus and 60 at base, 140 in total |
| 33.00 USD, other category | any | 0 | 33 | 49.5, rounded down to 49 |

If the 57.80 USD purchase is later refunded by half, half of its 228 points, that is 114 points, are removed.
